items.title: Rossano Sportiello interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 2, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I mean think of Errol Garner. Errol Garner never went on stage knowing what he was going to play you know.

ctx.x: Well I wouldn’t say much of that, because I am one of those players that is very much inside the harmony, even though I like very much almost everything in the history of jazz. But you see I specialized from Fats Waller to Teddy Wilson, and then the bebop, and then of course as a piano player I fell in love with the Bill Evans world. And that’s my thing is tonal jazz, so far. Then maybe one day I will feel the necessity to go in other directions. But for example, what I try always to explain to the audience is…

important, to be in the moment. You know, don’t go — in my opinion, I don’t want to go on stage with a preconceived set list that is going to happen, this and this and this. Because it takes away all the fun of it. The most beautiful feeling is when you get in front of the piano and the audience and you are blank. And you have to figure out what’s the right tune to play to make the people happy and yourself happy. And this was the approach that some of the greatest players used. I mean think of Errol Garner.…

I can’t think of a better way to say it. That was fantastic what you just said. I wonder how the bass players used to talk amongst themselves about, “hey have you played with Errol? What was that like for you?”
